seo.title: Best Tea Houses in Antwerp (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Antwerp's top 12 tea houses, from traditional Belgian to trendy spots. Find your perfect brew, high tea, or cozy afternoon experience in 2026.

hero.subtitle: Antwerp offers a delightful array of tea houses, blending traditional elegance with modern charm, perfect for a relaxing afternoon or a indulgent high tea experience.

picks.name: The Tea Lab
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The Tea Lab is a modern oasis in the heart of the historic center, celebrated for its extensive menu of loose-leaf teas from around the world. Beyond the exceptional brews, their house-made cakes and savory bites are crafted with an artisan touch, making it ideal for a sophisticated afternoon tea or a quick, elegant stop.
picks.whatToOrder: Matcha Latte with a slice of their seasonal Cheesecake.
picks.insiderTip: They offer tea-tasting flights; ask their knowledgeable staff for recommendations based on your preferences.
picks.redditQuote: "The Tea Lab has such a chill vibe and their Earl Grey is seriously next level. Always stop by when I'm in Antwerp!"

picks.name: Pekfabriek
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in the trendy 't Groen Kwartier, Pekfabriek offers an industrial-chic setting with an unparalleled high tea experience. Their multi-tiered displays are laden with delicate sandwiches, warm scones with clotted cream and jam, and an array of exquisite miniature pastries. It's a perfect spot for celebrations or a luxurious afternoon.
picks.whatToOrder: The Full High Tea menu, complete with prosecco if you're feeling fancy.
picks.insiderTip: Reservations for high tea are highly recommended, especially on weekends, as they book up quickly.
picks.redditQuote: "Pekfabriek's high tea is an absolute treat. The space is beautiful and the food is just divine, worth every penny!"

picks.name: Maison Tartine
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Maison Tartine brings a touch of Parisian charm to Antwerp, specializing in beautifully crafted open-faced sandwiches (tartines) alongside a selection of fine teas. It's a cozy spot perfect for a light lunch or a comforting afternoon snack, with fresh ingredients and a welcoming atmosphere that feels like a step into a French bistro.
picks.whatToOrder: A savory Tartine 'Chèvre et Miel' with a classic Earl Grey tea.
picks.insiderTip: Their daily soup special is often a hidden gem, perfect to pair with a tartine on a cooler day.
picks.redditQuote: "Love Maison Tartine for a relaxed lunch. Their tartines are amazing and they have some really nice herbal teas."

picks.name: Konditori
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Konditori offers a slice of Scandinavia in Antwerp's Zuid district, known for its minimalist design and focus on high-quality baked goods. While popular for coffee, their tea selection perfectly complements their delicious cinnamon buns (kanelbullar) and rye bread sandwiches. It's a bright, airy space ideal for fika (Swedish coffee/tea break).
picks.whatToOrder: Kanelbullar (cinnamon bun) with a refreshing Scandinavian herbal tea.
picks.insiderTip: Visit early in the morning for the freshest pastries right out of the oven.
picks.redditQuote: "Konditori's kanelbullar are seriously addictive, and their tea makes it the perfect fika spot. So hygge!"

picks.name: Koffieklap
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Koffieklap is a beloved local favorite, known for its warm, inviting atmosphere and delicious homemade treats. While 'koffie' is in the name, their tea selection is equally thoughtful, offering a comforting range of black, green, and herbal infusions. It’s the perfect spot to unwind, chat with friends, or enjoy a quiet moment with a good book.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic English Breakfast tea with their famous homemade apple pie.
picks.insiderTip: They often have unique seasonal specials on their cake menu, so always check the display counter.
picks.redditQuote: "Koffieklap feels like a second home. The staff are lovely and their carrot cake with a pot of Earl Grey is my go-to comfort."

picks.name: Mooy
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mooy is Antwerp's most Instagram-friendly tea house, famous for its pastel pink interior and beautifully presented dishes. While known for brunch, they offer a curated selection of teas that pair perfectly with their fluffy pancakes, avocado toasts, and vibrant smoothie bowls. It’s an energetic spot for a stylish tea break.
picks.whatToOrder: Their 'Pink Cloud' tea (a fruity herbal blend) with the Berry Pancake Stack.
picks.insiderTip: Go during off-peak hours (late afternoon) to avoid the brunch rush and get the best photos.
picks.redditQuote: "Mooy is super cute for brunch and photos, but their tea selection is surprisingly good too! Definitely get the pancakes."

picks.name: Confiserie Elise
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Confiserie Elise is a timeless Antwerp institution, renowned for its exquisite Belgian chocolates and traditional pastries. Stepping inside feels like going back in time to an era of refined indulgence. Enjoy a pot of classic black tea served with a selection of their artisanal pralines or a delicate slice of their rich chocolate cake.
picks.whatToOrder: A strong Ceylon tea paired with a small box of assorted Belgian pralines.
picks.insiderTip: Ask about their seasonal truffle flavors; they are often limited editions and highly sought after.
picks.redditQuote: "Confiserie Elise is my guilty pleasure. Nothing beats their hot chocolate, but their simple tea and praline combo is pure class."

picks.name: Tinsel
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tinsel brings a fresh, healthy vibe to the Zuid district, focusing on organic ingredients and wholesome dishes. Their tea menu features a thoughtful selection of organic infusions, herbal blends, and classic options, perfectly complementing their range of salads, sandwiches, and vibrant breakfast bowls. It’s a bright and airy space ideal for a light, guilt-free treat.
picks.whatToOrder: An organic Green Tea with their famous 'Loaded Avocado Toast'.
picks.insiderTip: They have excellent vegan and gluten-free options clearly marked on the menu.
picks.redditQuote: "Tinsel is my go-to for a healthy brunch and their teas are surprisingly good. Very fresh and light atmosphere."

picks.name: Cuperus Espresso Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While primarily a celebrated coffee roaster, Cuperus takes its tea just as seriously, offering a carefully curated selection of high-quality loose-leaf teas. Their minimalist, industrial-chic setting provides a perfect backdrop for appreciating the nuanced flavors of a well-brewed cup. It's a great spot for tea purists who appreciate quality over frills.
picks.whatToOrder: A single-origin Oolong tea or their exquisite Sencha green tea.
picks.insiderTip: Don't hesitate to ask their baristas for recommendations; they're very knowledgeable about their tea selection.
picks.redditQuote: "Everyone raves about Cuperus' coffee, but their tea is seriously underrated. So good and the vibe is perfect for working."

picks.name: Wafelhuis Van Hecke
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A true Antwerp classic, Wafelhuis Van Hecke has been serving traditional Belgian waffles for decades right near the cathedral. While their Liege and Brussels waffles are the star, they offer a simple yet satisfying range of teas to accompany these iconic treats. It's a no-frills, authentic experience perfect for tourists and locals alike looking for a sweet fix.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic Brussels Waffle with powdered sugar and a simple Black Tea.
picks.insiderTip: Go for the Brussels waffle if you prefer a lighter, crispier texture; Liege waffles are denser and sweeter.
picks.redditQuote: "You HAVE to go to Wafelhuis Van Hecke for the real deal. Simple tea and the best waffles in Antwerp. End of story."

picks.name: Bakkerij Goossens
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Bakkerij Goossens is more than just a bakery; it's an Antwerp legend, known for its incredible bread and pastries since 1935. While seating is limited to a few stand-up tables, you can grab a simple, comforting cup of tea alongside a freshly baked 'roggebrood' (rye bread) or a 'boterkoek' (butter cake). It’s an authentic, budget-friendly spot for a quick tea and snack.
picks.whatToOrder: A hot Black Tea with a warm 'boterkoek' (butter cake).
picks.insiderTip: They only accept cash, so be prepared! Go early for the best selection of freshly baked goods.
picks.redditQuote: "Bakkerij Goossens is my secret spot for a cheap, delicious tea and a pastry. Their bread is legendary, even just a simple slice."

picks.name: Maison Gribouille
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Maison Gribouille is a chic French patisserie in the stylish Zuid district, offering an exquisite selection of cakes, tarts, and macarons that are as beautiful as they are delicious. Their refined ambiance makes it a perfect setting for a more luxurious afternoon tea, where artfully crafted desserts are paired with premium loose-leaf teas.
picks.whatToOrder: A pot of Darjeeling tea with a selection of their delicate macarons or a fruit tart.
picks.insiderTip: Their window displays are often seasonal works of art; take a moment to admire them.
picks.redditQuote: "Maison Gribouille is where I go when I want to feel fancy. Their cakes are unreal and the tea service is very elegant."

faq.question: What is 'high tea' in Antwerp, and how is it different from afternoon tea?
faq.answer: In Antwerp, 'high tea' typically refers to a more substantial meal served in the late afternoon, often including savory items like sandwiches and quiches, alongside scones and pastries. While the term 'afternoon tea' might suggest a lighter affair, many establishments in Belgium use the terms interchangeably to describe a similar spread. Always check the menu specifics when booking.

faq.question: Are reservations required for tea houses in Antwerp?
faq.answer: For popular high tea experiences, especially at places like Pekfabriek, reservations are highly recommended, sometimes even essential, particularly on weekends. For casual tea and a pastry, walk-ins are usually fine, but it's always a good idea to check the venue's website or call ahead during peak tourist seasons or for larger groups.

faq.question: Do Antwerp tea houses offer vegan or gluten-free options?
faq.answer: Many modern tea houses and cafes in Antwerp, such as Tinsel and The Tea Lab, are increasingly offering vegan and gluten-free options for both their teas and accompanying pastries or snacks. It's best to check with the individual establishment beforehand, especially if you have severe dietary restrictions, to ensure they can accommodate your needs.

faq.question: What are the typical operating hours for tea houses in Antwerp?
faq.answer: Most tea houses in Antwerp generally open around 9:00 AM or 10:00 AM and close in the late afternoon, usually between 5:00 PM and 6:00 PM. Some may have extended hours on certain days or for special events. Always verify the current opening hours directly with the specific tea house you plan to visit, as they can vary.

faq.question: Can I buy loose-leaf tea to take home from these establishments?
faq.answer: Yes, several tea houses and specialty stores in Antwerp, including The Tea Lab and Cuperus Espresso Bar (which, despite its name, has a great tea selection), offer a range of loose-leaf teas for purchase. This is a fantastic way to bring a taste of your Antwerp experience home with you. Don't hesitate to ask staff for recommendations.

faq.question: What is the price range for a typical tea experience in Antwerp?
faq.answer: The price for a tea experience in Antwerp can vary widely. A simple tea and pastry at a bakery like Bakkerij Goossens might cost €5-€10. A more elaborate afternoon tea with cakes and sandwiches at a mid-range tea house could be €15-€25 per person. For a full, luxurious high tea experience with multiple courses, expect to pay €25-€40+ per person.

methodology: Our selection of Antwerp's best tea houses is based on extensive local research, online reviews, and expert recommendations. We prioritized venues offering high-quality tea, distinctive atmospheres, and exceptional culinary pairings, ensuring a diverse range of options for every preference.
